Q3847510.summary: In this venerated icon the Virgin, veiled in deep blue with a star on her shoulder, holds the Christ Child on her arm against a gold ground; the Child, in a light tunic, raises his right hand in blessing and looks up toward his mother. Both now wear silver crowns, recalling the icon's solemn coronation in 1955. Long honoured as the patroness of Manfredonia, the icon is carried in procession through the city each year on 31 August.
facts: Legend says the icon was painted in Constantinople in the 5th century and brought to Siponto, but historians date the panel to around the 11th century; the first certain records date from 1327.
A fire in 1872 destroyed the lower part of the panel, and later restorations (1896, 1927, 1964) left it extensively repainted; it was restored again in 2010–2011.
It was solemnly crowned on 28 August 1955 by Cardinal Angelo Roncalli, the future Pope John XXIII.

Q3847510.notes: The 4th-century date in the source data reflects legend; the work should move out of the 1st–7th century range (c. 11th century). The Commons photo was taken during the 2008 procession; since 2002 a copy by Aronne Del Vecchio has been carried in procession, so the photograph may show the copy rather than the original panel.
